# API Contract Checklist: Backend Conventions and API Foundation

**Purpose**: Validate that the requirements for the shared error contract, status mapping, no-leak rules, request-validation semantics, JSON 404, and conventions documentation are complete, clear, consistent, and measurable before planning and implementation.
**Created**: 2026-11-07
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Error Contract Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are the structural fields of an error response (code, message, optional details) explicitly specified as a single shared contract? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the shape of each error detail (path + message) defined, including what the path represents? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK003 Is it stated that the error contract is the single source of truth and must not be redeclared by any module? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the full set of error codes enumerated, with no code left implicit or open-ended? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the behaviour for an unrecognized/invalid error code specified (rejection by the contract)? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK006 Are the reserved-but-unexercised codes (UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, RATE_LIMITED) documented with their intended downstream purpose so their presence is not ambiguous? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions]

## Status Map Correctness

- [ ] CHK007 Is each error code mapped to exactly one HTTP status, with the mapping stated unambiguously? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK008 Does every enumerated code in FR-002 have a corresponding status in the FR-003 mapping (no code without a status, no status without a code)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002 vs §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK009 Are the specific status values (400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 413, 429, 500) individually assigned rather than described only as "appropriate status"? [Measurability, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK010 Is there a single documented mechanism for raising a typed application error carrying code, message, and optional details? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003]

## No-Leak and Security Rules

- [ ] CHK011 Is it explicitly required that server-fault (500) responses expose no original message, stack trace, detail list, or secret? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK012 Is "no leak" defined concretely enough to be objectively verified (named forbidden contents rather than a vague "safe" adjective)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-005, §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the logging policy specified for each class of error (4xx not logged; only 500-class logged)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK014 Is it stated that secrets must never appear in logs or error messages, independent of the response body rule? [Coverage, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK015 Are the generic 500 code and generic message requirements defined so the fallback body is deterministic? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, §FR-005]

## Error-Mapping Coverage

- [ ] CHK016 Are the translation rules for each failure source (explicit 4xx app error, schema violation, malformed JSON, oversized body, everything else) individually specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK017 Is the catch-all requirement clear that any non-mapped or non-standard thrown value becomes a generic 500? [Coverage, Spec §FR-004, §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK018 Is the uncommon-parser-failure boundary (unsupported media type, aborted request) explicitly declared as out of scope / defaulting to 500, rather than left undefined? [Edge Case, Spec §Assumptions, §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK019 Is the already-sent-headers scenario addressed in the requirements (delegate rather than re-send)? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]

## JSON 404 Behaviour

- [ ] CHK020 Is the unknown-route requirement specified to return the shared error shape with code NOT_FOUND? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK021 Is it explicit that the JSON 404 replaces the framework default non-JSON/HTML 404? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, User Story 1 Scenario 2]
- [ ] CHK022 Is it stated that a 404 response still carries the standard security and CORS headers? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Validate Semantics

- [ ] CHK023 Is it specified that validation covers any combination of body, params, and query, each against its own schema? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK024 Is the timing requirement clear that validation runs before the controller executes? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007, §FR-008 constitution Principle I]
- [ ] CHK025 Is the failure behaviour defined with part-prefixed detail paths and aggregation of all failing parts? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007, User Story 2 Scenarios 1 & 5]
- [ ] CHK026 Is the success behaviour defined (controller receives parsed, typed, sanitized values with unknown keys removed)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007, User Story 2 Scenarios 2 & 4]
- [ ] CHK027 Can "typed" and "sanitized" be objectively verified from the stated acceptance scenarios? [Measurability, Spec §User Story 2]
- [ ] CHK028 Are missing-body / wrong-content-type-with-body-schema cases addressed in the requirements? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Reference Module (Health)

- [ ] CHK029 Is the requirement that the health endpoint's path and response body remain unchanged stated unambiguously? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008, User Story 3 Scenario 1]
- [ ] CHK030 Is it specified that the health response continues to validate against the existing shared health-response contract? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK031 Is the health endpoint's role as the documented reference module explicitly defined? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, User Story 3]

## Conventions Documentation

- [ ] CHK032 Are the required topics for the conventions document enumerated (module layout, naming, layering, REST/JSON, error-code table, validate usage, pagination, testing, logging/security)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK033 Is it required that the documentation stay consistent with delivered code (every referenced symbol, path, and status matches)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009, User Story 3 Scenario 2]
- [ ] CHK034 Is the requirement to update repository guidance files to reflect colocated tests and error-raising rules specified? [Coverage, Spec §FR-009, User Story 3 Scenario 3]
- [ ] CHK035 Is the pagination convention clearly marked as documented-only (no implementation this round)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, §Assumptions]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK036 Are the success criteria measurable (percentages/counts) rather than qualitative claims? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001–§SC-006]
- [ ] CHK037 Is the "tests run with no env file and no database" requirement stated as an objective, verifiable condition? [Measurability, Spec §FR-010, §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK038 Is the red→green test expectation tied to every error-producing behaviour, with each error test asserting contract conformance? [Coverage, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK039 Is the "no new dependencies" and bounded-diff-size constraint quantified enough to be checked objectively? [Measurability, Spec §FR-012, §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK040 Does every functional requirement trace to at least one acceptance scenario or success criterion? [Traceability, Spec §Requirements vs §User Scenarios/§Success Criteria]

## Consistency & Ambiguity Sweep

- [ ] CHK041 Are the terms "error contract", "application error", and "validation" used consistently across spec sections without drift? [Consistency, Spec §Requirements, §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK042 Do the out-of-scope assumptions (auth, rate limiting, logging stack, pagination code, OpenAPI, web-side parsing) agree with the reserved codes and documented-only items elsewhere in the spec? [Conflict, Spec §Assumptions vs §FR-002/§FR-009]
- [ ] CHK043 Is the body-size limit referenced consistently (no conflicting thresholds) across requirements and edge cases? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, §User Story 1 Scenario 4]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
